Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The recruiting team seeks to build the culture of Stripe by aligning the strongest global talent to our highest impact business needs. They focus on bringing Stripe’s operating principles to life in their recruiting processes, providing the highest-quality candidate experience, and leveraging data driven storytelling to influence the business.

What you’ll do

To further this important mission, we are looking for a consultative and creative recruiter to grow and scale our Business & Core teams in APAC. You can expect high impact and wide-ranging responsibilities: owning full-cycle recruiting, driving hiring strategy, and delivering best-in-class candidate experience. This person must be a builder who thrives in a learning environment—unafraid to try new things, embrace new ideas, and welcome suggestions for how we can iterate on our processes.

Responsibilities

  • Fulfill junior level and high volume requisitions, scaling up teams across Stripe Delivery Center in India, Bangalore 
  • Partner with multiple internal stakeholders with varying priorities to understand their hiring objectives and drive recruiting strategies to hit headcount goals
  • Partner closely with recruiting analytics to ensure accurate reporting of hiring progress back to the business
  • Build and drive cross-functional partnerships with compensation, human resources, finance and others to scale hiring across Stripe
  • Consistently generate a healthy pipeline of high quality candidates by driving initiatives across branding, events, and employee referral channels
  • Provide timely reporting of key metrics and insights to drive decisions and improve processes

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 4+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience (in-house experience strongly preferred)
  • Strong track record in target achievements, experience managing high volume hiring in fast moving environment 
  • Experience partnering with hiring teams throughout the recruiting process, acting as an effective hiring partner and trusted advisor 
  • High agency, can handle ambiguity in a fast-moving organization, and thrives on a high level of autonomy and responsibility
  • Proven abilities to attract passive candidates and build a diverse pipelines
  • An active and data driven approach to problem solving; you enjoy making sense of the trends and using the insights to better your process to make it more efficient
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence stakeholders internally and externally

Preferred requirements

  • Experience with India market hiring 
  • Experience with reporting work, proficient in data tools such as Visier, Greenhouse Reports, GoodTime, Gem etc 
  • Ability to quickly adopt new recruiting technologies, AI and optimize workflows for scale
descriptions.job-10zu10c:
DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

About the Team

We are a fast-moving and progressively-thinking team that intimately collaborates with traders and quantitative researchers to implement, refine and deploy alpha signals, evaluate and maintain trading tools, improve our research pipeline, while ensuring that our code bases remain nimble, maintainable and extensible.

We embed deeply with our customers to solve high-impact, complex problems.

We move quickly when we prototype, and we tread lightly when we ship to production.

We operate at the intersection of ensuring customer success and creating quality products that stand the test of time.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer, you will be an integral member of a systematic trading team comprised of experienced technologists, quantitative researchers, and traders. You will:

  • Work directly with researchers to implement research studies, simulate trading strategies, and develop algorithms to compete in financial markets.
  • Embed with trading desks, work intimately with traders and portfolio managers, learn about their problem spaces, extract domain models, and build ergonomic, performant and extendable engineering solutions
  • Collaborate with other engineering teams to accelerate the research lifecycle from strategy prototype to production deployment
  • Evaluate new technology and improve our technology stack on a continuous basis

What you bring to the team:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
  • A minimum of 2+ years’ experience using Python in a production setting
  • A strong understanding of quantitative finance and mathematics
  • Experience with linux-based, large-scale, concurrent, high-throughput, low-latency software systems
  • A track record of working directly with end customers, scoping and delivering production systems in fast-moving and ambiguous environments
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills - you communicate clearly with stakeholders as well as other engineers, fostering a collaborative, supportive working environment.
  • Experience with low-level systems programming languages (C/C++, Rust, Zig) is a plus
  • Experience with functional programming is a plus

The annual base salary range for this position is $175,000 to $225,000, depending on the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and relevant skill set. The position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.  In addition, DRW offers a comprehensive suite of employee benefits including group medical, pharmacy, dental and vision insurance, 401k (with discretionary employer match), short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, health savings accounts, and flexible spending accounts.

For more information about DRW's processing activities and our use of job applicants' data, please view our Privacy Notice at https://drw.com/privacy-notice.

California residents, please review the California Privacy Notice for information about certain legal rights at https://drw.com/california-privacy-notice.
descriptions.job-1q232os:
Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

You generate pipeline for our account executives (AEs) in the markets where dollar access is hardest. Most of it happens in person, at conferences and the events around them. In between, you find the next targets and make sure every lead lands with the right AE.

You also own the numbers behind the top of the funnel and use them to recommend where the team spends its time next, including which new markets are worth testing. You'll help shape how we run Growth, with real autonomy and a scope that grows with what you show.

Your First Six Months

  • Months 1-2: Learn the product, our ICP and how we sell to banks and fintechs. Shadow our sales conversations, and get to know our stack, our playbooks and the way we operate. Go to your first conference with the team: help with pre-booking, work the floor alongside our Sales and Growth teams, and book your first meetings. By the end of month two, you can pitch Augustus on your own.

  • Months 3-4: Execution is yours. Own a conference end to end, from the target list to the follow-up: book the meetings, route each one to the right AE and make sure it happens. Take meetings on your own and work closely with Sales and Marketing.

  • Months 5-6: Own the pipeline for a set of markets and run your first event. You've turned what you've learned into data: which conferences, intros and markets bring deals that close, and which don't. You sync with the rest of GTM to bring in what they see and use it to shape our market strategy: where we go next, how we go in, who we target first and what we lead with.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

This role is for you if:

  • You're outgoing and at your best in front of people. You can start a conversation with a stranger at a booth and hold it with a bank's CFO.

  • You do what needs to be done, even when it's not glamorous: building a prospecting list, chasing a follow-up, carrying boxes to the booth.

  • You think clearly and work from data. You take an unstructured dataset and come back with answers and insights.

  • You're diligent and organised. Nothing falls through the cracks.

  • You use AI to move fast, but don't trust the output blindly. You check results, question the systems and don't ship anything you wouldn't put your name on.

  • You're curious: when something takes too long, you find a faster way to do it.

  • After every conference, you know what you'd do differently next time, and you do it.

This is not for you if:

  • You'd rather work behind a screen than in front of people. Most of our pipeline starts with a conversation in person.

  • You want a well-defined scope and clear processes. Ours change as we grow, and you'll help build many of them.

  • You want a predictable week. Plans change, the bar is high and the hours are long.

  • You expect your degree to count for more than your results.

Hard Requirements

  • You are currently pursuing or have obtained, in the last two years, a Bachelor's or Master's degree from a stellar institution.

  • You have 1-2 previous internships or roles in high-growth startups, venture capital, private equity, consulting or investment banking, and/or you have demonstrated initiative through side projects, student organizations or entrepreneurial experiences.

  • Fluent English. Spanish is a strong plus.

  • You can travel regularly, often at short notice.

  • Based in Berlin or willing to relocate.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate's experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual base salary range for this role is €60,000-€80,000 + equity and benefits.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.

Augustus is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.

Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

Location:

  • Remote - US / Canada

About the role:

Browsers are steadily closing the door on how device identity has worked on the web. Sardine's Device Intelligence & Behavior Biometrics team builds the signals that tell genuine users apart from fraudsters, bots, and AI agents, and we need an engineer to own how our Web SDK identifies devices reliably across Safari, Firefox, Chrome, Brave, and in-app WebViews, and how it reaches the browser as a true first party.

You will own the Web SDK, its client-side identity storage, and the CDN reverse proxy integrations that sit in our customers' traffic. This is a production engineering role with a strong investigative side: much of the work starts with understanding exactly how a browser treats a cookie, a request, or a domain, and ends with shipping a change that keeps working for thousands of end users.

What You Will Do

  • Lead our move to privacy-resilient first-party integrations: opt-in CHIPS partitioned cookies, true first-party cookie flows, and in-band CDN reverse proxy integrations.

  • Build and extend reverse proxy integrations across CDNs and origin setups (Cloudflare, AWS Lambda@Edge / CloudFront, Fastly, Akamai, F5, NGINX), including per-customer randomized paths for SDK loading and event ingestion.

  • Modernize the SDK's client-side identity storage layer, and design graceful degradation when persistence is limited.

  • Design device identity handoff between our native mobile SDKs and in-app WebViews, resistant to spoofing and abuse.

  • Instrument and measure device identifier longevity and churn by browser, version, and integration mode, and alert on regressions.

  • Track browser privacy changes (ITP, ETP / dFPI, CHIPS, Storage Access API, tracker lists) ahead of release, and turn them into SDK and integration decisions.

  • Own the performance, bundle size, and reliability of an SDK that runs on login, signup, and payment flows of fintechs and enterprises.

  • Work with backend (Go), mobile, dashboard, and customer success teams to roll out changes across existing customers without breaking installs.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 3 years building production JavaScript / TypeScript that runs in the browser.

  • Strong TypeScript / JavaScript and deep knowledge of browser APIs, cross-browser differences, and WebView behavior.

  • Deep, practical knowledge of cookie and storage behavior across browsers: SameSite, partitioning, CHIPS, ITP / ETP, CNAME cloaking detection, and eviction rules.

  • Experience shipping and maintaining a third-party JavaScript SDK or library that runs on other companies' sites.

  • Experience building or operating reverse proxies or edge functions in production.

  • Solid web networking fundamentals: HTTP, CORS, cookies, DNS, TLS, caching, CDNs.

  • Good judgment on effort, risk, and migration paths in systems with many external integrators.

  • Clear written and verbal communication of trade-offs to engineering, product, and customer-facing teams.

  • Experience with at least one popular web framework or library, such as React, Angular, Vue.js, Next.js, or Svelte. Experience with multiple frameworks is a plus.

  • Experience with modern JavaScript development tools and build systems, including Node.js, npm, Babel, and bundlers such as Webpack, Vite, or Rollup. Familiarity with one or more of these tools is preferred.

Nice to Have

  • Background in fraud prevention, bot detection, device fingerprinting, or web security.

  • Go experience.

  • Experience with JavaScript obfuscation, anti-tampering, or reverse engineering minified code.

  • Familiarity with automation frameworks (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium) and how they differ from real browsers.

  • Experience with iOS (Swift) or Android (Kotlin / Java) SDK development, including WebViews and native to web bridges.

  • Public work such as browser bug reports, open source, blog posts, or talks.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and release automation, using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins, to automate the building, testing, versioning, and deployment of SDKs or web applications

Tech Stack

  • Web SDK: TypeScript

  • Edge: Cloudflare, AWS (Lambda@Edge / CloudFront), Fastly, Akamai, NGINX, F5

  • Backend: Go

  • Infrastructure: GCP / AWS

Benefits we offer:

  • Generous compensation in cash and equity

  • Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

  • Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

  • Flexible paid time off and Year-end break

  • Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

  • 4% matching in 401k / RRSP - US and Canada specific

  • MacBook Pro delivered to your door

  • One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.

  • Monthly meal stipend

  • Monthly social meet-up stipend

  • Annual health and wellness stipend

  • Annual Learning stipend

Join a fast-growing company with world-class professionals from around the world. If you are seeking a meaningful career, you found the right place, and we would love to hear from you.

To learn more about how we process your personal information and your rights in regards to your personal information as an applicant and Sardine employee, please visit our Applicant and Worker Privacy Notice.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. About the team

User Policy Operations evaluates businesses against Stripe’s Terms of Service and related policies. We help Stripe support businesses responsibly while protecting our users, financial partners, and the broader Stripe ecosystem.

What you’ll do

As a Team Lead in User Policy Operations, you’ll lead and develop a team of operations associates responsible for policy evaluations and risk assessments. You’ll combine people leadership with hands-on involvement in complex cases, helping the team make well-supported decisions and deliver consistent operational results.

Minimum Qualifications

We are seeking

Bitdeer (NASDAQ: BTDR) is looking for an experienced transactional attorney to join our U.S. Legal team in San Jose, California as Senior Legal Counsel, Power & Land. Bitdeer acquires, energizes and builds data center and power infrastructure across multiple U.S. states and in Alberta, Canada. This role owns the legal work that moves a site from a land position to an energized facility: acquisitions, leases and easements; water rights and supply; utility, interconnection and energy management arrangements; long-lead electrical equipment; and the entitlements and regulatory approvals each site depends on.

This is a dedicated power and land role in our U.S. legal function, so you will own the portfolio rather than support it. You will work directly with site selection, development, construction, energy and procurement leaders, bring in and direct specialist and local counsel where state and local law requires it, and build the form agreements, diligence standards and obligation tracking that this work depends upon.

What you will be responsible for

  • Lead land and site transactions end to end — purchase and sale agreements, ground and build-to-suit leases, options, easements and rights-of-way, title and survey review, title insurance, restrictive covenants, water rights and supply agreements, and post-closing obligations.
  • Negotiate the utility and power arrangements that make a site viable: interconnection and transmission agreements, discretionary and distribution service agreements, substation and shared facilities agreements, energy management and retail supply arrangements, and the financial security, milestone and energization obligations inside them.
  • Advise on interconnection strategy and queue position with transmission and distribution service providers, electric cooperatives and system operators — including ERCOT, PJM and TVA territories and the Alberta market — and on large-load thresholds, study processes and cost allocation.
  • Support site selection and diligence: zoning and land use, entitlements and permitting, environmental review, utility and water availability, and the tax incentive, abatement and special district structures that determine whether a site clears.
  • Lead the land use and entitlement workstream with local counsel — rezoning and text amendments, moratoria, variances, and public hearings — and prepare the business for the public and political dimension of those proceedings.
  • Paper and negotiate procurement of long-lead electrical infrastructure such as transformers, switchgear and substation equipment, including origin representations, substitution and walk-away rights, and compliance with bulk-power-system and trade-control requirements.
  • Partner with the construction team on the interface between site, power and EPC paper, so interconnection milestones, energization dates and construction schedules are consistent across documents rather than negotiated separately.
  • Serve as a legal point of contact for utilities, cooperatives, landowners, developers, and state and local authorities, and select and manage specialist and local counsel in each market on scope, quality and spend.

Rain makes the next generation of payments possible across the globe. We’re a lean and mighty team of passionate builders and veteran founders. Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

The role

We're hiring a Product Compliance Manager to make sure every product Rain ships is compliant by design. You'll sit between Product, Engineering, Legal and Compliance, turning regulations and card network rules into clear product requirements before code is written, not after launch.

Rain moves fast: partners go live in weeks, and new products like embedded wallets, credit and prepaid programs, and agent-issued virtual cards keep coming. You'll own the compliance review that lets that speed hold up with regulators, the networks, our bank partners and auditors.

What you'll do

  • Own product compliance reviews. Assess new products, features and partner programs end to end, from PRD to launch, and sign off on the compliance requirements each one needs.

  • Translate rules into requirements. Turn regulations and network rules into concrete specs, controls and acceptance criteria that Product and Engineering can build against.

  • Keep card programs network-compliant. Own adherence to Visa and Mastercard operating rules as a Principal Member, including program approvals, network registrations and periodic attestations.

  • Cover consumer protection. Apply Reg E, Reg Z, TILA, UDAAP, ECOA and state requirements to cardholder agreements, disclosures, fees, rewards and dispute flows.

  • Review partner programs. Assess partner use cases, marketing materials, cardholder terms and onboarding flows before launch, and monitor them after.

  • Partner with Financial Crimes. Make sure KYC/KYB, sanctions screening and transaction monitoring requirements are built into products such as wallets, payouts, onramps and offramps.

  • Track the landscape. Follow stablecoin, payments and money transmission developments in the US and abroad, including federal stablecoin rules and MiCA, and flag what changes our roadmap.

  • Build the program. Maintain product compliance policies, the review process, a product risk inventory and the evidence trail that bank partners, networks, regulators and auditors ask for.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in product compliance, regulatory compliance or a similar role at a fintech, card issuer, program manager, sponsor bank or payments company.

  • Hands-on knowledge of card issuing: Visa and/or Mastercard operating rules, prepaid and credit programs, and the issuer–processor–program manager model.

  • Working knowledge of US consumer financial regulation, including Reg E, Reg Z, UDAAP and state money transmission rules.

  • A track record of reviewing products before launch and writing requirements that engineers actually build from.

  • Sound judgment on risk: you know when to say "yes, if" and when to say no, and you can explain both.

  • Clear writing for very different readers, from an engineer's ticket to a bank partner's due diligence questionnaire.

Nice to have, but not mandatory

  • Experience with stablecoins, digital assets or crypto-linked card programs.

  • Exposure to international regimes such as MiCA, UK FCA rules or APAC payments licensing.

  • Background at a Principal Member issuer or sponsor bank, including network audits or bank partner exams.

  • Familiarity with BSA/AML, OFAC and FinCEN requirements.

  • A JD or a certification such as CAMS or CRCM.

  • Comfort reading API docs and working inside tools like Linear, Jira or Notion.

Things that enable a fulfilling, healthy, and happy experience at Rain:

  • Unlimited time off 🌴 Unlimited vacation can be daunting, so we require Rainmakers to take at least 10 days off.

  • Flexible working ☕ We support a flexible workplace. If you feel comfortable at home, please work from home. If you’d like to work with others in an office, feel free to come in. We want everyone to be able to work in the environment in which they are their most confident and productive selves. New Rainmakers will receive a stipend to create a comfortable home environment.

  • Easy to access benefits 🧠For US Rainmakers, we offer comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents, as well as a 100% company subsidized life insurance plan.

  • Retirement goals💡Plan for the future with confidence. We offer a 401(k) with a 4% company match.

  • Equity plan 📦 We offer every Rainmaker an equity option plan so we can all benefit from our success.

Stripe’s Tax Transfer Pricing team designs, implements, and defends the intercompany pricing policies that support Stripe’s global operating model, ensuring pricing between Stripe entities is compliant, defensible, and aligned with how the business creates value.

As Stripe expands its product portfolio and international footprint, our transfer pricing policies and documentation must evolve alongside the business. Transactions between Stripe affiliates are becoming increasingly complex and, in some cases, share characteristics with transactions commonly undertaken by financial services institutions. These arrangements, including those supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities, may also be subject to scrutiny from regulators that oversee the financial services sector. We are seeking an experienced Transfer Pricing Specialist with financial services expertise to help develop practical, scalable transfer pricing policies, work through the tax and regulatory considerations relevant to intercompany arrangements, and provide subject matter expertise in audit defense and dispute resolution.

What you’ll do

The Financial Services Transfer Pricing Strategist will be a hands-on, collaborative member of the team responsible for developing and implementing compliant, practical transfer pricing policies and processes. The role will focus on transactions between Stripe’s legal entities that have characteristics commonly associated with the financial services sector, including intercompany arrangements supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities.

This individual will work closely with teams across the organization and must be an excellent communicator who can explain complex transfer pricing concepts clearly to non-tax audiences. The ideal candidate will have transfer pricing experience in payments, fintech, banking, or another regulated financial services environment, as well as a track record of partnering effectively with cross-functional teams and other members of the tax organization.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with teams within and outside of Finance to develop, execute, and maintain transfer pricing policies for Stripe’s current and future operating structure and product offerings with a strong moral compass and integrity

  • Build relationships with product and business leaders to understand their organizational structure and activities, and adapt transfer pricing policies in response to changes
  • Assist finance, legal, and tax teams in government and regulatory audits, and support Stripe’s participation in tax audits, advance pricing agreements, and competent authority proceedings

Minimum requirements

  • A bachelor’s degree or higher in accounting, economics, business, law, or a related field, and 10+ years of relevant experience
  • Strong knowledge of global transfer pricing laws and regulations, experience with international tax planning for a multinational, and experience in financial services, banking, fintech, payments, or another regulated industry
  • Experience managing transfer pricing documentation and compliance; practical experience with transfer pricing dispute resolution, including audits, advance pricing agreement negotiations, and competent authority negotiations; and experience developing, maintaining, and implementing intercompany agreements
  • Knowledge of financial accounting concepts, including accounting for intercompany transactions; professional experience with Excel, Oracle, and Smart View; and enjoyment of working with and digging into data from multiple sources
